analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation only. cli-reference.md changes the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a `--prompt-prep` benchmark row (head line 572). That row is outside the visible units except through the patch. docs/reference/configuration.md adds a 'Prompt preparation and admission' table (head lines 587-596) with DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE, _MB, _VERIFY, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_TEMPLATE_LOOPS and a truncated DARKBLOOM_TTFT_COLD_LOAD_RELEASE row. I reviewed cli-reference.md lines 827-1807 (paths, env passthrough, fan, logout, report, prefix-cache sections) and found no changed security claims. No source code is supplied, so no control is weakened in the evidence.

Open questions for later passes:
(1) The docs describe a new in-process prompt-token piece cache scoped to 'the request's prefix-cache scope' and disabled by the global DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0. It reuses tokenization results across requests, so it could add a cross-request TTFT timing signal (T-041 / SEC-035, A-001). Confirm in the code that the scope key is the coordinator-authored cacheSalt, that no cross-account sharing is possible, and that the kill switch is honoured. T-041 affected_files and detection_hint do not yet cover PromptTokenCache.swift. Update the threat model if the cache holds prompt-derived content in memory.
(2) The configuration.md rows say 'Forwarded by LaunchAgent', but the cli-reference passthrough table (lines 1734-1753) and its 'only these variables' statement (line 1695) do not list the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_* variables. This is documentation drift, not a security regression. Verify against LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvKeys.
(3) The _VERIFY background re-tokenization is described as disabling reuse on mismatch. Confirm it fails closed and cannot cause unbounded CPU work (T-010/T-029 availability).
(4) The configuration.md patch excerpt is truncated and the final row is unseen.

No finding is raised because no code or enforceable behaviour change is visible.
